cards.back: The study of the economy as a whole, including national income, employment, and inflation
Gross Domestic Product - the total market value of all final goods and services produced in a country
Gross National Product - GDP plus net income from abroad
GDP measured at current prices
GDP adjusted for inflation, measured at constant prices
A measure of the price level used to convert nominal GDP to real GDP
A sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services
A sustained decrease in the general price level of goods and services

cards.front: What is the Consumer Price Index (CPI)?
cards.back: A measure of the average change in prices of consumer goods and services
The percentage of the labor force that is unemployed
Unemployment due to workers searching for jobs or transitioning between jobs
Unemployment due to a mismatch between skills and job requirements
Unemployment due to economic downturns and business cycles

cards.front: What is the natural rate of unemployment?
cards.back: The unemployment rate that exists when the economy is at full employment
The total demand for goods and services in an economy at a given price level
The total supply of goods and services in an economy at a given price level
The recurring pattern of economic expansion and contraction
A period of declining economic activity, typically defined as two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth
A severe and prolonged recession
An increase in real GDP over time
Government policy regarding taxation and spending to influence the economy
Central bank policy regarding money supply and interest rates to influence the economy
Increasing government spending or decreasing taxes to stimulate the economy
Decreasing government spending or increasing taxes to slow down the economy
Increasing money supply or decreasing interest rates to stimulate the economy
Decreasing money supply or increasing interest rates to slow down the economy
The magnified effect of an initial change in spending on total output

cards.front: What is the crowding out effect?
cards.back: When government spending reduces private investment
The inverse relationship between unemployment and inflation
A situation of high inflation and high unemployment occurring simultaneously
The total amount of money in circulation in an economy

cards.front: What is the velocity of money?
cards.back: The rate at which money circulates in the economy

cards.front: What is the quantity theory of money?
cards.back: MV = PY (Money supply × Velocity = Price level × Real GDP)
The price of one currency in terms of another currency
When imports exceed exports
When exports exceed imports
The ability to produce a good at a lower opportunity cost than another country
The ability to produce more of a good with the same resources than another country
